newsitem.title: USA: U.S. officials see little impact from Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: U.S. officials see little impact from Deng's death.

text.p: The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday will probably have little effect on the functioning of the country, U.S. officials said.

There was no immediate formal reaction in Washington to Deng's death, but State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said he expected that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would go ahead with an already planned trip to China next week.
President Bill Clinton was informed of Deng's death while he was having lunch during a visit to Boston. White House officials said he would issue a statement shortly.

Davies told reporters the State Department had only just concluded, based on official Chinese press reports, that Deng had died. "So any follow-on decisions to be made have yet to be made, but we are proceeding on the assumption that the visit to Beijing will go ahead, and we expect it will," he said.
A senior U.S. official said Deng, 92, "had in recent years detached himself from the day-to-day levers of powers, was no longer making decisions, clearly."

"So as regards the functioning of China this will likely not have a great effect," said the official, speaking on condition he was not identified. But the official said this was "an important moment" for the Chinese because Deng had been a seminal figure in China's communist revolution and, more recently, the architect of the country's economic reforms.
